advances: This classifies parameter limits and the actual centroid multipliers under joint variation of the positive fibers. Buffered bad-attainment additionally needs a base-depth choice in the complement of a limiting zero face.

proof:
The affine span of every $C_K$ is $\operatorname{aff}P\times\mathbb R^d$ since every sampled fiber has interior. If $m_K$ were on the relative boundary, there would be a nonzero relative supporting affine function nonnegative on $C_K$ and zero at $m_K$. Its integral against $\mu_K$ would be zero, so by positivity and continuity it would vanish on every fiber. Its continuous coefficient would vanish and its base affine restriction would vanish on the spanning set $P$, a contradiction. Therefore $m_K$ is relative interior. Both $C_K$ and $m_K$ vary continuously with $K$: convex hulls of finitely many Hausdorff-convergent compact sets converge, and bounded integrals of fiber indicators and coordinate times indicator converge by their almost-everywhere convergence. The relative inradius centered at $m_K$ is the minimum of $h_{C_K}(u)-u\cdot m_K$ over the unit sphere in the relative linear span, so it is continuous and positive on $\mathcal A$. Its minimum is $\rho>0$. An affine $h\ge0$ with mean one has $h(m_K)=1$. Testing the ball in the direction of steepest decrease bounds its linear coefficient by $1/\rho$. Boundedness of $m_K$ then bounds its constant coefficient.

Select a body subsequence and, by this coefficient bound, a coefficientwise convergent subsequence of $h_j$. The limit $h$ is nonnegative by Hausdorff convergence and still has mixed mean one by bounded integration. Writing $A_j=\int L_j\,d\mu_{K_j}$, the normalization is exactly $A_j=(\int h_j^{-r}\,d\mu_{K_j})^{1/r}$. If $h$ is positive on $C_K$, the $h_j$ are uniformly bounded below on $C_{K_j}$ for large $j$, so the integral and scale converge to the corresponding finite positive values for $h$. Then $L_j=A_jh_j$ converges to a positive normalized parameter.

If $h$ vanishes on the hull, its minimum over the hull equals its minimum over the compact union of actual fibers, so it vanishes on some sampled fiber. Apply the inverse-power boundary divergence lemma to that moving fiber with the same exponent and restricted affine coefficients. Its integral tends to infinity, forcing $A_j\to+\infty$. If the continuous coefficient is nonzero, $h$ is nonconstant on every full-dimensional fiber and is positive on every fiber interior. Its value at the centroid of each limiting fiber is its strictly positive mean there. Centroid and coefficient convergence then give $L_j(z,g_{j,z})\to+\infty$ for all $z$. If the continuous coefficient vanishes, $h$ is nonnegative affine on the base hull with mean one and minimum zero. Its zero set is a nonempty proper exposed face, and at each sampled $z$ outside it the same argument gives divergence.
statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, let $P$ be a fixed nonempty finite base, and let $\mathcal A$ be a compact family in the simultaneous Hausdorff metric of tuples of positive convex $d$-fibers $K_z$, $z\in P$, of total volume one, with every fiber volume at least $v>0$ and all fibers contained in a fixed ball. Use mixed measure $\mu_K=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes(\mathbf 1_{K_z}\,dX)$, its centroid $m_K$, and $C_K=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_z(\{z\}\times K_z)$. There is $\rho>0$ such that every $C_K$ contains the relative $\rho$-ball about $m_K$. Hence the affine functions $h\ge0$ on $C_K$ with $\int h\,d\mu_K=1$ have relative linear coefficient norm at most $1/\rho$ and uniformly bounded constant coefficients in fixed relative affine coordinates.

Fix $r\ge d$. For every sequence $K_j\in\mathcal A$ and affine $L_j>0$ on $C_{K_j}$ with $\int L_j^{-r}\,d\mu_{K_j}=1$, there is a subsequence with $K_j\to K\in\mathcal A$ and $h_j=L_j/\int L_j\,d\mu_{K_j}$ converging coefficientwise to an affine $h\ge0$ on $C_K$ of mixed mean one. If $h>0$ on $C_K$, then $L_j$ converges coefficientwise to a finite positive normalized affine parameter on $C_K$. Otherwise $\int L_j\,d\mu_{K_j}\to+\infty$. In this second case, write $g_{j,z}$ for the actual centroid of $K_{j,z}$. If $h$ has nonzero continuous coefficient then $L_j(z,g_{j,z})\to+\infty$ for every $z\in P$. If its continuous coefficient vanishes, its base zero set is a nonempty proper exposed face $F$ of $\operatorname{conv}P$ and the same divergence holds for each $z\in P\setminus F$.
title: The normalized affine parameter limit and centroid divergence alternative
